Cause: The new trainer pod (trainer-q3-full-...) is Unschedulable because its CPU request is larger than any node in the cluster. The pod requests cpu: 16 (and memory: 24Gi) per container, but your general node pool is m6i.2xlarge with only 8 vCPU per node — and allocatable is slightly less than capacity because system daemons reserve some of it [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-5]. A pod whose request exceeds every node's capacity will never schedule [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

Evidence:
- Pod condition PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message "0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient cpu."
- Pod spec resources.requests: cpu "16", memory "24Gi" (limits identical).
- Last week's successful run (trainer-q2-full-...) requested only cpu 6 / memory 20Gi, which fits on an 8 vCPU / 32 GiB node.
- No preemption victims available, so priority/preemption will not help here.

Fix (pick one, applied by the job owner):
1. Lower the trainer pod's cpu request to something that fits an 8 vCPU node (e.g. 6, as last week's job used). Remember node allocatable is less than the full 8 vCPU because of system reservations [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-5]. This is the quickest unblock.
2. Or add a larger-instance node pool (e.g. m6i.4xlarge or bigger) and schedule the job onto it — adding nodes with sufficient capacity is the documented remedy when the pod legitimately needs more than current nodes offer [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-1].

You can confirm per-node allocatable headroom with `kubectl describe nodes` [cite: concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers#my-pods-are-pending-with-event-message-failedscheduling-2].
